title: Find Diameter Endpoints of a Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, represented by edges, return a binary string indicating whether each node is an endpoint of any diameter path.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, represented by edges, return a binary string indicating whether each node is an endpoint of any diameter path. A diameter path is the longest path between any two nodes, and an endpoint is the first or last node on such a path.
constraints: 1≤n≤100,000 and edges is a valid undirected tree.
Return one character per node: one iff it can end some longest path.
A one-node tree marks its only node.
hints: Find endpoints A and B of any diameter using two breadth-first searches.
A node is an endpoint of some diameter exactly when its distance from A or from B equals the diameter length.
Run BFS from both endpoints and mark that condition for every node.
Tree eccentricity satisfies max(dist(A,v),dist(B,v)); it equals the diameter precisely for possible diameter endpoints.
editorial: Tree eccentricity satisfies max(dist(A,v),dist(B,v)); it equals the diameter precisely for possible diameter endpoints.

tests.explanation: Nodes zero and two end the unique diameter, producing 101.
Every leaf can pair with another leaf on a diameter, producing 0111.
